key_insight: A nonhydrostatic ocean model is extended with a moving generalized vertical coordinate that can switch among z-level, terrain-following, isopycnal, or hybrid layers to better capture realistic 3D ocean dynamics on unstructured grids.
engineering_relevance: This improves the fidelity and robustness of simulations for stratified coastal flows and internal waves where traditional vertical coordinates can struggle with accuracy, stability, or boundary-layer representation.
method: Built a nonhydrostatic, unstructured C-grid ocean model with generalized vertical coordinates (GVC).
Added a conservative momentum advection scheme and a positivity-preserving layer-height method for unstructured meshes.
Applied the hybrid-coordinate formulation to internal solitary waves and bottom boundary layer instability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against turbulent channel flow and comparative simulations showing that hybrid vertical coordinates outperform z- or terrain-following coordinates for internal solitary waves.
watch_item: The approach adds algorithmic complexity, so careful implementation is needed to preserve conservation and positivity on moving, unstructured layers.
paper_title: An unstructured-grid, nonhydrostatic, GVC ocean model Part I: Model description and application of vertical hybrid coordinates to internal solitary waves
